description: Feed in your requirements — free-form concerns, questions, whole areas of interest — and get back your requirements grouped and disambiguated into well-formed watched topics, then checked BY CODE, topic by topic, against what we actually read: a topic is offered as a Watch ONLY when a desk, a Watch we keep or a standard Watch reads it from sources with a recent item. How recent is not a fixed number: the live bar is derived from the topic's own cadence and served with each answer in `coverage.basis.bars.liveDays`, beside `coverage.rule`, which states it in words. Every topic carries `coverage` — its state (covered, gap, or cannot-check with the reason), the sources, how many and how fresh. Gaps come back under `coverageRequests`, each with the free propose_topic call that asks us to start keeping it; `coverage.summary` says it in one line. A model proposes the topics; it never decides what is offered. The count is disclosed in BOTH directions: overlaps are merged, broad requirements are split into the separate daily reports they actually need, and `billing.expansion` states the requirement-to-topic ratio outright so a split is as visible as a merge. Large requirements are resolved in batches, so a requirement the desk cannot place does not sink the rest: `partial: true` and `unresolvedRequirements` name what it could not place and why — never a topic invented to cover a gap. Nothing here is a price: Watches are free. Configure, save and keep a Watch at no charge: no card, no end date. Up to 5 saved Watches per verified email or key. Need more, or something built around your own question? Ask us. Pass the covered topics to save_watch (domain + topics) to keep them. Needs no contact details. Real model work: ~10 per day per network address (shared egress shares the allowance).

requirements.description: What you want watched, in your own words — one blob of text or bullet points; the desk does the grouping
